literal_meaning: ঘাড় থেকে ভূতকে নামানো (to make a ghost descend from the neck)
figurative_meaning_en: To stop someone from an unjust or unreasonable demand
similar_in_english: Get the monkey off one's back
Talk someone out of a bad idea
example_sentences_in_bangla: বাচ্চাটার ঘাড় থেকে ভূত নামাও, সে এত আবদার করছে না।
উসকানিটা তার ঘাড় থেকে ভূত নামিয়ে দাও।
example_sentences_in_english: Get that ghost off the kid's neck; he's just throwing a tantrum.
Help him shake off that bad influence from his neck.
history: This idiom draws from Bengali folk beliefs in ghosts (bhoot) possessing people, often metaphorically for irrational behavior, rooted in rural superstitions.
note: The idiom reflects cultural views on possession as a metaphor for stubbornness or undue persistence.
